source.title: Effect of Weight Quantization on Learning Models by Typical Case Analysis
source.authors: Shuhei Kashiwamura; Ayaka Sakata; Masaaki Imaizumi

record.tranche_reason: The study analytically and numerically tests generalization-error behavior across the sample-to-dimension ratio in quantized linear regression, a different setting and method from the deep-network studies.
record.gate_note: The study's own double-descent results are in Figure 5 and Appendix Figure 9. The paper also cites double-descent results from other work; those citations are not recorded as rows. Figure 4 and Figure 10 vary quantization hyperparameters rather than the double-descent axis, and Figure 6 compares replica analysis with AMP rather than testing double descent, so those results are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study derives its own generalization-error curves for quantized linear regression, extending double descent to a new setting. Its sample-to-dimension sweeps bear on V3 and V4, and its noise comparison bears on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases Section 4.3 and the conclusion: quantization shifts the peak toward smaller M/N, so more parameters are needed to reach the regime where overparameterization reduces error. The authors attribute this qualitatively to a reduced effective parameter count; they do not demonstrate V5 or V7.
record.recipe_differences: Uses typical-case replica analysis and AMP for quantized linear regression rather than the original deep-network settings. It studies the sample-to-dimension ratio and quantization effects.
record.method_sensitivity: The peak location varies with quantization; the paper reports a shift toward smaller α than ridge regression. The appendix reports a diminished peak at low noise. The paper also says the shift tendency is marginally more pronounced for non-uniform quantization and that this discrepancy disappears with larger ω.

fits_no_version.finding: Quantization shifts the peak toward smaller M/N, interpreted by the authors as reducing the effective number of parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization can delay the onset of the beneficial overparameterized regime.

record.problems: The double-descent curves are presented as plots without numeric curve values or uncertainty estimates. The comparison varies the asymptotic ratio α=M/N rather than isolating sample count at fixed dimension. Figure 5's caption gives α=N/M, whereas the main text defines α=M/N.
record.rows_left_out: No reported double-descent conditions were left out. Figure 4 and Figure 10 results concern quantization hyperparameters rather than the double-descent axis; Figure 6 concerns AMP validation rather than double descent.

untested.parts: Fall-rise-fall behavior over training epochs; AMP convergence experiments do not test this.
A finite-dimensional experiment adding observations to a fixed model; the evidence is an asymptotic learning curve parameterized by M/N.
Universality across model classes and direct verification of an exact training-interpolation threshold for the quantized models.
Prediction of peak locations across size, epochs, and samples by a single measured effective-complexity quantity.
Variance decomposition, triple or multiple descent, and disappearance of the peak under optimally tuned regularization.
Replotting risk against an effective parameter count to recover an ordinary U-shaped curve.

record.verdict_notes: Use α=M/N, as defined in the setup, analysis, axes, and Section 4.3; Figures 5 and 9 invert this ratio in their captions. A proportional-limit ratio sweep is legitimate evidence for an asymptotic sample learning curve, so the absence of a finite fixed-dimension experiment alone does not justify limits_scope for V3. Numerical ordinates are unnecessary for the explicit qualitative conclusions, but the supplied text cannot justify assigning the same state to every ω-specific curve. The low-noise reduction supports V6; untested regularization and multiple-peak clauses do not limit it. All reported double-descent conditions are already represented or declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network model-size sweeps and the specified fall-peak-fall pattern as deep-network size grows.
The study sweeps the asymptotic ratio α=M/N, not sample count at fixed model dimension; it does not establish the effect of adding samples while holding other quantities fixed.
The tested class is quantized linear regression, not a broad sweep across multiple model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study compares low- and high-noise settings. It does not test multiple or triple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization eliminates the peak.
The study does not replot risk against an effective number of parameters to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

source_check.notes: Figures 5 and 9 have caption typos giving α=N/M; their axes, Section 3, and Section 4.3 establish α=M/N. The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate; individual ω curve values and shapes remain unreadable from the supplied figure text.

statements.correction: Appendix A, Figure 9: σ=0.01, b=9.0, λ=0.01; uniform and non-uniform quantization; diminished double-descent peak; no stated failure of recovery; V4 limits_scope.
statements.problem: The quantized-regression facts and conditions are correct, but placing this result under challenges overstates the evidence: a diminished peak does not establish absent or reversed recovery.

statements.correction: Section 4.3: collective description of the peak shifting toward smaller α=M/N; no direct quantized training-interpolation-threshold verification. Figure 5: individual ω curve shapes not recoverable from the supplied text. Section 6: future work on AMP divergence from the theoretical limit and practical hyperparameter selection.
statements.problem: The exact quantized training-interpolation threshold is not directly verified, but the paper does not explicitly list this gap. Its stated future work concerns AMP failing to achieve the theoretical limit and practical hyperparameter selection.
